summary: This chunk adds two new files: a red-team report on a session-cache design for a checkout service, and a short user_notes.md on how the run was produced. The report finds the design unsafe: an 8GB cache would consume all the shared Redis cluster's free memory (meltdown risk), and invalidation only covers promo changes, leaving stale prices for catalog/tax changes. It lists 12 ranked findings (2 Critical, 4 High, 6 Medium) with failure scenarios, root causes, fixes, a 5-step minimum-changes path, verification items for 4 'Plausible' findings, and a retest checklist. user_notes.md explains the Write tool was blocked for report.md (written via heredoc instead) and that em dashes were kept despite a no-em-dash rule.

claims.text: 8GB cache footprint (200k sessions x 40KB) equals the cluster's entire stated free memory, before per-key overhead or growth
Catalog price changes and tax-rate changes have no invalidation path; only the promo_changed event is handled
Invalidation uses KEYS session:*:pricing followed by bulk DEL, both blocking Redis commands on a shared cluster
Delete-all invalidation causes a synchronized stampede of downstream calls plus an ~8GB Redis rewrite burst
The cache's kill switch (feature flag) is served from the same cluster the cache can melt down, so it cannot be used to mitigate its own incident
The design defines zero hit/miss/fallthrough/eviction metrics and no alerts
A five-step minimum-changes path (version-stamped invalidation first) closes the top findings, with step 1 closing four root causes
All 12 raw findings cited the artifact accurately and fell inside the charter's scope; only one merge occurred (into F-4)
The Write tool was blocked for report.md, so it was written via shell heredoc instead; charter.md wrote normally
Em dashes were kept in report/charter prose for format fidelity, overriding the CLAUDE.md no-em-dash rule

risks.note: The 'killed findings: none, 12 raw -> 12 final' reconciliation is asserted but the underlying raw findings/merge process aren't shown in this chunk to check against.
Deviating from the CLAUDE.md no-em-dash rule is justified by 'format fidelity' but no rule or authority is cited establishing that format fidelity should override the project convention.

least_confident: Whether the finding-count bookkeeping (12 raw findings, 1 merge, 1 seam-sweep addition, 0 killed, 12 final) is internally consistent, since the raw pre-merge findings and the merge/kill process aren't shown in this chunk.
